description:
SOUNDNESS-CRITICAL COMPARATOR SURFACE: this TODO's work touches
benchbox/core/equivalence/cross_surface.py (covered by .github/CODEOWNERS as
`benchbox/core/equivalence/** @joeharris76`) and
benchbox/core/tpchavoc/equivalence.py (adjacent to, and sharing the same
waiver-baseline discipline as, benchbox/core/tpchavoc/validation.py, which
IS covered as `benchbox/core/**/validation.py @joeharris76`; note that
tpchavoc/equivalence.py itself is not literally matched by an existing
CODEOWNERS glob - verified against the current 3-line .github/CODEOWNERS -
but should be treated as soundness-critical and reviewed by the code owner
regardless). Its PR will require code-owner review before merge.

Verified by reading both modules on this branch: no known-divergence waiver
entry, in either file, carries any date or expiry field.
  - cross_surface.py's `known_divergences: dict[str, str | ClassifiedDivergence]`
    (CrossSurfaceGate field, line 371) holds bare strings (e.g.
    `_READ_PRIMITIVES_KNOWN_DIVERGENCES`, cross_surface.py:859-885) and
    `ClassifiedDivergence` instances (cross_surface.py:338-357, e.g.
    `_H2ODB_KNOWN_DIVERGENCES` at 813-816, `_CLICKBENCH_TIE_AMBIGUOUS` at
    619-624+) - neither the `str` nor the `ClassifiedDivergence` dataclass
    (fields: `reason`, `accepts`, `requires_live_divergence`) has a date field.
  - equivalence.py's four engine-keyed baselines (`KNOWN_DIVERGENCES`,
    `POSTGRES_KNOWN_DIVERGENCES`, `DATAFUSION_KNOWN_DIVERGENCES`,
    `CLICKHOUSE_KNOWN_DIVERGENCES`, all `dict[str, str]`) are plain
    key->reason-string maps with no date field either.

The only existing staleness signal in either module is "stale-baseline
failure": a waiver whose divergence has stopped reproducing is caught (in
cross_surface.py's `_report`, the `resolved` check at line ~1188-1192; in
equivalence.py's shared `_report`, a `resolved` PRINT only - see the sibling
TODO tpchavoc-duckdb-gate-vacuity-guard w3 for that gap). But a waiver whose
divergence is STILL LIVE (e.g. an "irreducible engine-semantic difference" or
an "approximate by construction" classification) never gets re-examined - it
can sit correct-when-written but stale-in-spirit indefinitely: the engine
version that produced the documented behavior may have changed, the
benchmark's data/queries may have evolved, or the original rationale may no
longer hold, and nothing forces a human to re-look.

This TODO adds a lightweight, OPTIONAL `review_by:` date to waiver entries
(both the bare-string form, by upgrading it to a small structured wrapper or
a side-table, and the `ClassifiedDivergence` form, as a new optional field),
and a warning-or-failure when a `review_by` date has passed, so long-lived
waivers are periodically forced back into review even when their divergence
never disappears on its own.

anti_patterns.dont: add review_by enforcement as a hard FAIL by default without checking it would not immediately break an existing gate
anti_patterns.why: a surprise new failure mode on merge day for a benchmark whose owner is not in the room is worse than a warning.

anti_patterns.dont: conflate review_by-past-due with the existing resolved-divergence stale-baseline failure
anti_patterns.why: they are different signals (one means 'the divergence is GONE, prune the entry'; the other means 'the divergence may still be valid but a human should re-look') and must not share one code path or one message format that a reader could confuse.

anti_patterns.dont: fork _report per module to add this
anti_patterns.instead: one keys on backend+query, the other on query+variant).
anti_patterns.why: both modules already have their own _report; extend each in place, do not introduce a third shared helper unless the two are trivially unifiable (they are not

anti_patterns.dont: make review_by mandatory on every waiver
anti_patterns.why: most waivers (e.g. the h2odb Q9 DECIMAL-scale residue, an inherent engine behavior) may never need re-review and forcing a date on them is busywork, not signal

deferrals.reason: Out of scope; this item only adds the detectable signal (a warning/failure at report time). Automating a proactive nudge is a separate CI/scheduling concern.
deferrals.summary: Automatically opening an issue/PR or paging an owner when a review_by date passes.

deferrals.reason: review_by is optional by design (per the task framing: 'Keep it lightweight'); mandating it on every existing entry is a larger migration this item does not need to force.
deferrals.resolved_reason: [G4 sweep] non-actionable: review_by is optional by design per the parent item's own framing; retroactively mandating it on all waivers was deliberately rejected.
deferrals.summary: Requiring review_by on every existing waiver retroactively.

preserves.behavior: The existing stale-baseline (resolved-divergence) failure behavior in both modules' _report functions is unchanged by this addition - review_by is a new, independent check, not a replacement.

cross_surface.py's GATES stay green and equivalence.py's tpchavoc-equivalence-report* targets stay green after this lands (no waiver in either module should already have an accidentally-past-due review_by introduced by this change).
review_by is OPTIONAL - every existing waiver entry with no review_by continues to behave exactly as today (no forced migration, no new failure for entries that omit it).

prior_art.concept: benchbox/core/equivalence/cross_surface.py:1173-1196 _report - where a new review_by warning/failure check is added, alongside the existing new/resolved/missing_backends/unclassified_empty checks.

benchbox/core/equivalence/cross_surface.py:338-357 ClassifiedDivergence - the dataclass to extend with an optional review_by field (or a documented decision not to, if the bare-string form is chosen as the carrier instead).

benchbox/core/equivalence/cross_surface.py:371 CrossSurfaceGate.known_divergences: dict[str, str | ClassifiedDivergence] - the Union type that must accommodate whatever wrapper form w1 chooses for bare-string entries with a review_by date.

benchbox/core/tpchavoc/equivalence.py:434-470 _report (KNOWN_DIVERGENCES/POSTGRES_KNOWN_DIVERGENCES/DATAFUSION_KNOWN_DIVERGENCES/CLICKHOUSE_KNOWN_DIVERGENCES, all dict[str, str]) - the second _report that needs the same review_by check, in a shape compatible with its plain string-valued dicts.

cross-surface-baseline-update-flag.yaml (planning) - a closely related, already-filed TODO for a --update-baseline flag to DROP resolved entries; this item is complementary (forcing review of LIVE entries) and should reuse its w0's re-confirm-the-live-file-and-lines discipline, not duplicate its writer.

work_units.notes:
DECISION, matching the open_questions defaults exactly (directed as the
policy for this batch and independently confirmed sound):
  (a) cross_surface.py: option (i) - added `review_by: date | None = None`
      as a third field on `ClassifiedDivergence`. Bare-`str` entries
      CANNOT carry a review_by (documented explicitly in both the
      dataclass docstring and the module's new "waiver review policy"
      section) - no bare-string waiver was converted to
      ClassifiedDivergence to add one. Verified this does not complicate
      the sibling read-primitives-waivers-classified-divergence TODO:
      `_READ_PRIMITIVES_KNOWN_DIVERGENCES` (read_primitives gate) still
      has its existing bare-string entries untouched; nothing in this
      change forces or blocks that sibling's future conversion.
  (b) equivalence.py (tpchavoc): option (ii) - a side-table
      `dict[str, date]` per baseline, keyed identically to the baseline
      it annotates (e.g. `CLICKHOUSE_KNOWN_DIVERGENCES_REVIEW_BY`), passed
      into the shared `_report` as a new optional `review_by` parameter.
      No existing `dict[str, str]` baseline's value type changed.
  (c) WARN, not fail - matches the default exactly. A past-due
      `review_by` prints a "WAIVER REVIEW DUE - ..." line in both
      modules' `_report`s but never changes the return code, kept
      deliberately distinct in wording and code path from the existing
      `resolved` GATE FAILURE (per the anti_patterns).
Prior notes (superseded by the decision above, kept for context):
Two open design questions to resolve before implementing:
  (a) Carrier shape for cross_surface.py's bare-`str` waivers (the majority
      of entries - see _READ_PRIMITIVES_KNOWN_DIVERGENCES, and any others
      not yet converted to ClassifiedDivergence by the sibling TODO
      read-primitives-waivers-classified-divergence). Options: (i) add
      `review_by` as a THIRD optional field on `ClassifiedDivergence` and
      require every review_by-bearing waiver to at least be wrapped in
      `ClassifiedDivergence(reason=..., accepts=lambda _: True, review_by=...)`
      even if it has no real predicate yet (accepts-everything is
      explicit, not implicit, in this form) - this reuses one type instead
      of two; or (ii) introduce a small side-table
      `dict[str, date]` (e.g. `_REVIEW_BY: dict[str, date]`) keyed by the
      same divergence key, checked independently of the waiver's own
      shape - avoids touching the `known_divergences` Union type at all.
      Prefer (i) if the sibling TODO's ClassifiedDivergence conversion is
      expected to land first (fewer bare strings to carry the concern for
      long-term); prefer (ii) if this item lands independently and should
      not force every bare-string waiver into a dataclass. State and
      justify the choice here.
  (b) Same question for equivalence.py's plain `dict[str, str]` baselines
      (KNOWN_DIVERGENCES et al.) - these have no ClassifiedDivergence
      equivalent at all today, so a side-table (ii)-style
      `dict[str, date]` per baseline, or a small `@dataclass` wrapper
      (`KnownDivergence(reason: str, review_by: date | None = None)`)
      replacing the bare `str` value type, is the realistic choice. Note
      this is a wider blast radius (touches every existing baseline
      entry's type) - if it proves too invasive for zero-value-change
      entries, the side-table is likely the pragmatic default.
  (c) Warn vs fail: decide in this work unit, do not defer. Given the
      module already treats a stale-baseline `resolved` divergence as a
      hard gate FAILURE in cross_surface.py (line ~1191), a past-due
      `review_by` on a STILL-LIVE waiver is a weaker signal (the waiver
      may still be entirely correct) - default to WARN (print prominently,
      do not fail exit code) unless a strong case for FAIL emerges (e.g.
      "the gate is meant to be a hard forcing function and a warning is
      too easy to ignore"). Record the decision and rationale.
work_units.summary: Design the review_by carrier for both waiver shapes and decide warn-vs-fail on a past-due date

work_units.notes:
Added `review_by: date | None = None` to `ClassifiedDivergence`. In
`_report`, computes `review_due = sorted(key for key, entry in
known.items() if isinstance(entry, ClassifiedDivergence) and
entry.review_by is not None and entry.review_by < date.today())` and, for
each, prints `"WAIVER REVIEW DUE - {key}: review_by {entry.review_by} has
passed - {entry.reason}"` - a distinct prefix from "GATE FAILURE" so a
reader (or a naive grep for FAILURE) cannot confuse the two signals. The
return statement (`1 if (new or resolved or missing_backends or
unclassified_empty) else 0`) is UNCHANGED - review_due never enters it,
per w1(c)'s warn decision.
work_units.summary: Implement the review_by field/side-table and wire the warning/failure check into cross_surface.py's _report

work_units.notes:
Added an optional `review_by: dict[str, date] | None = None` parameter to
the shared `_report` (equivalence.py). Computes `review_due = sorted(key
for key, due in review_by.items() if key in known and due <
date.today())` and prints the same "WAIVER REVIEW DUE - ..." line style as
cross_surface.py (message text intentionally parallel, code NOT shared -
per the anti_patterns, the two `_report`s stay separate functions).
Verified live all four report modes after the change: DuckDB hard gate
(220/220, exit 0), DataFusion sample (206/206, exit 0), ClickHouse sample
(195/202 + 7 classified, exit 0, no review-due warning since the worked
example's date is not yet past), Postgres sample unreachable in this
environment (clean SKIP, exit 0, unaffected - POSTGRES_KNOWN_DIVERGENCES
is empty so review_by never applies there regardless).
work_units.summary: Implement the review_by field/side-table and wire the equivalent check into equivalence.py's shared _report

work_units.notes:
Added a "Waiver review policy" paragraph to both module docstrings
(cross_surface.py, after the "Currently gated" paragraph; equivalence.py,
after the LIMIT-stripping paragraph) stating: an entry MAY carry an
optional review_by date; a past-due date WARNS (never fails); this is
independent of and does not replace the existing stale-baseline
(`resolved`) failure - one means "the divergence is gone, delete the
entry", the other means "the divergence may still be valid, re-look
anyway". Also added matching explanatory paragraphs to the `ClassifiedDivergence`
dataclass docstring and both `_report` docstrings.
work_units.summary: Document the policy in both modules' docstrings
